title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page is a set-theoretic preliminary ('sorites ensemblistes', 14.6.86) for the chapter GF V 'Algèbre des figures'. Let L be a set and 𝔏 ⊂ 𝔓(L) a family of subsets. Grothendieck defines the support |𝔏| = ∪_{A∈𝔏} A. For A ∈ 𝔏 he defines a combinatorial 'boundary' ∂A = ∪{B ∈ 𝔏 : B ⊊ A} and an 'interior' A° = A \ ∂A. He also sets 𝔏_x = {A ∈ 𝔏 : x ∈ A}.

Key observation. x ∈ A° exactly when A is a minimal element of 𝔏_x.

Proposition 1. The following are equivalent.
(1) For every x (implicitly x ∈ |𝔏|), 𝔏_x has a smallest element, written A(x).
(2) Two conditions hold:
  α) for all A, B ∈ 𝔏, A∩B is the union of the members of 𝔏 contained in A∩B;
  β) every x ∈ |𝔏| lies in some minimal element of 𝔏_x, i.e. ∪_{A∈𝔏} A° = |𝔏|.
(3) With 𝔏' = {A ∈ 𝔏 : A° ≠ ∅}, three conditions hold:
  γ) the 'open cells' A°, A ∈ 𝔏', form a partition of |𝔏|;
  δ) every A ∈ 𝔏 is saturated for that partition, i.e. is a union of cells;
  η) if A ∈ 𝔏', B ∈ 𝔏 and A° ⊂ B, then A ⊂ B.

Margin note (NB). δ and η can be replaced by the single condition δ'): every A ∈ 𝔏 equals ∪_{B∈𝔏, B⊂A} B°. A second marginal note points to a finer variant 'à dextre' in GF VIII p. 37.

Proof. The proof on the next page runs 1⇒2⇒3⇒1 and is straightforward.

What it is in modern terms. It characterises when a family of 'closed figures' behaves like the closed cells or closed strata of a cell or stratified decomposition. The interiors partition the support. Each closed figure is a union of interiors. Closure inclusion is detected by the interiors. Equivalently, x ↦ A(x) is a well-defined map from |𝔏| to the poset 𝔏', whose fibres are the cells A°.

This is the familiar picture of:
- the face poset of a regular cell or polyhedral complex;
- equivalently, a map to a poset with its Alexandrov topology, where the A(x) play the role of minimal closed neighbourhoods.

The purpose is to set up a combinatorial 'algebra of figures', presumably finite unions of polyhedral or semi-algebraic pieces, stratified by their open faces.
errors: Condition 1° is stated 'pour tout x ∈ L'. It must be x ∈ |𝔏|: for x ∉ |𝔏| the set 𝔏_x is empty and has no smallest element.
Condition β is written '∀ x ∈ 𝔏'. It should read ∀ x ∈ |𝔏|.
Both are only notational slips. The proposition and its proof (next page) are correct.
The marginal claim that γ + δ' can replace γ + δ + η is also correct. If x ∈ A°, A ∈ 𝔏', and x ∈ B, then δ' gives C ⊂ B with x ∈ C°; uniqueness in γ forces C = A, so A ⊂ B.

ideas.what: Combinatorial interior/boundary of a member of a family of sets, A° = A minus the union of strictly smaller members; the cells A° partition the support exactly when each point has a smallest containing member.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset / cell stratification; minimal closed neighbourhoods (Alexandrov topology); a stratification as a map to a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies; the face-poset formalism of regular CW complexes (Björner and others); 'stratified spaces over a poset' in later homotopy theory (Lurie, Higher Algebra appendix)
ideas.where_published: The broad theme of tame or dévissage stratifications appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6. This particular sorite is not published.

ideas.what: Equivalence between 'smallest containing member exists' and 'intersections are unions of members plus interiors cover the support'.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but elementary set-theoretic lemma, the standard face-poset/cell-partition characterisation. Its only interest is documentary: it is the opening of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 'Algèbre des figures' (GF) notes, and it refers forward to GF VIII.
transcription_corrections: 'Soient L un [?]' is most likely 'Soient L un ensemble'.
Under condition η, the marginal 'i.e. A ∈ 𝔏'' glosses 'A° ≠ ∅'. It is not a separate statement.
Left margin reads roughly 'Voir variante « à dextre » (?) plus fine dans GF VIII p. 37 ...'; the reading is uncertain.
In β, '∀ x ∈ 𝔏' is what is written, but the meaning is ∀ x ∈ |𝔏|.
